```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(targets)

manifest <- tar_read(data_manifest)
flow <- tar_read(dataset_flow)
grain <- tar_read(grain_all)
units <- tar_read(unit_summary_all)
coverage <- tar_read(coverage)
missingness <- tar_read(missingness)
numeric_summary <- tar_read(numeric_summary_all)
level_summary <- tar_read(level_summary_all)
outcomes <- tar_read(outcome_registry)
exposures <- tar_read(exposure_registry)
settings <- tar_read(settings)

fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
id_order <- function(x) factor(x, levels = unique(x[order(as.numeric(x))]))
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10))
```

A rough working report, rebuilt whenever the data change.
Every number comes from pipeline targets, and nothing here shows a row of data.
Dataset IDs are shown and names are not.

## The data this report describes

```{r}
#| label: manifest-summary
tibble::tibble(
  ` ` = c(
    "Datasets included",
    "Participants",
    "Observations (participant by wave)",
    "Rows including extra screen-time measures",
    "Overall data hash"
  ),
  Value = c(
    fmt(nrow(manifest)),
    fmt(sum(manifest$participants)),
    fmt(sum(manifest$primary_rows)),
    fmt(sum(manifest$rows)),
    unique(manifest$overall_hash)
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The hash changes when any included dataset's harmonised data change.

## Dataset flow

```{r}
#| label: flow
flow |>
  mutate(across(c(datasets, participants, rows), \(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", fmt(x)))) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Stage", "Datasets", "Participants", "Observations"), align = "lrrr")
```

Datasets identified or requested but never given a spec are not recorded in the repository, so the top of the flow diagram has to be added by hand.

## Size and concentration

```{r}
#| label: concentration
by_size <- manifest |>
  arrange(desc(participants)) |>
  mutate(
    rank = row_number(),
    share = participants / sum(participants),
    cumulative = cumsum(share)
  )
top <- function(k) pct(sum(head(by_size$share, k)))
```

The five largest datasets hold `r top(5)` of participants, and the ten largest hold `r top(10)`.
The median dataset has `r fmt(median(manifest$participants))` participants.

```{r}
#| label: fig-concentration
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-cap: "Cumulative share of participants, datasets ordered from largest to smallest."
ggplot(by_size, aes(rank, cumulative)) +
  geom_step() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Datasets, largest first", y = "Share of participants")
```

```{r}
#| label: size-table
by_size |>
  transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_id,
    Participants = fmt(participants),
    Observations = fmt(primary_rows),
    Waves = waves,
    `Share of participants` = pct(share)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrr")
```

## Stage 1 units

A unit is one dataset in one wave in one country.
Rows aged `r settings$age_limit` or over, and rows with no age, are not eligible.

```{r}
#| label: units
units <- units |> mutate(too_small = age_eligible < settings$min_unit_rows)
tibble::tibble(
  ` ` = c(
    "Units",
    "Datasets with more than one unit",
    paste0("Units with fewer than ", settings$min_unit_rows, " eligible rows"),
    "Share of rows aged 19 or over or with no age",
    "Share of rows with no age"
  ),
  Value = c(
    fmt(nrow(units)),
    fmt(sum(table(units$dataset_id) > 1)),
    fmt(sum(units$too_small)),
    pct(1 - sum(units$age_eligible) / sum(units$rows)),
    pct(sum(units$age_missing) / sum(units$rows))
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-unit-size
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-cap: "Eligible rows per unit (log scale). The line marks the provisional minimum unit size."
ggplot(filter(units, age_eligible > 0), aes(age_eligible)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = settings$min_unit_rows, linetype = 2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "Eligible rows in the unit", y = "Units")
```

## Ages and collection years

```{r}
#| label: fig-age
#| fig-height: 11
#| fig-cap: "Age range of each dataset: full range (thin line) and the middle of its units' median ages (point)."
age <- units |>
  filter(!is.na(age_min)) |>
  summarise(
    age_min = min(age_min),
    age_max = max(age_max),
    age_mid = weighted.mean(age_median, rows),
    .by = dataset_id
  )
ggplot(age, aes(y = reorder(dataset_id, age_mid))) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = age_min, xmax = age_max), colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(x = age_mid), size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = settings$age_limit, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Age in years", y = "Dataset")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-year
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: "Observations by collection year."
units |>
  filter(!is.na(year_median)) |>
  mutate(year = round(year_median)) |>
  summarise(rows = sum(rows), datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = year) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, rows)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "Collection year (unit median)", y = "Observations")
```

## Demographics

```{r}
#| label: demographics
demo_vars <- c("sex", "ses_household", "urbanicity", "minority", "indigenous", "sample_population")
level_summary |>
  filter(variable_name %in% demo_vars, st_measure_id == "primary") |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = c(variable_name, level)) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n), .by = variable_name) |>
  arrange(variable_name, desc(n)) |>
  transmute(Variable = variable_name, Level = level, Observations = fmt(n), Share = pct(share), Datasets = datasets) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr")
```

Countries: `r n_distinct(na.omit(units$country))`, with `r sum(is.na(units$country))` units that record no country.

```{r}
#| label: countries
units |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), rows = sum(rows), .by = country) |>
  arrange(desc(rows)) |>
  head(25) |>
  transmute(Country = coalesce(country, "(not recorded)"), Datasets = datasets, Observations = fmt(rows)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr", caption = "The 25 countries with most observations.")
```

## Coverage

A value counts when it is neither missing nor `Unknown`.

```{r}
#| label: coverage-by-domain
coverage |>
  filter(n_value > 0) |>
  summarise(
    variables = n_distinct(variable_name),
    datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id),
    .by = domain
  ) |>
  arrange(domain) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Domain", "Variables with data", "Datasets with any"))
```

```{r}
#| label: coverage-plot-fn
coverage_plot <- function(domain_name) {
  d <- coverage |>
    filter(domain == domain_name, n_value > 0) |>
    mutate(dataset_id = id_order(dataset_id))
  ggplot(d, aes(dataset_id, variable_name, fill = share)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent, name = "Non-missing") +
    labs(x = "Dataset", y = NULL, title = domain_name) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 5),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}
plot_height <- function(domain_name) {
  n <- n_distinct(coverage$variable_name[coverage$domain == domain_name & coverage$n_value > 0])
  1.5 + 0.11 * n
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-coverage-screen
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 11
coverage_plot("screen_time")
```

## Missingness

Missing and `Unknown` cells are sporadic when their wave has real values on that variable, and systematic when the wave has none.
Only sporadic missingness is a candidate for imputation.

```{r}
#| label: missingness
schema_domain <- distinct(coverage, variable_name, domain)
missingness |>
  left_join(schema_domain, by = "variable_name") |>
  summarise(
    cells = sum(rows),
    value = sum(n_value),
    sporadic = sum(n_sporadic),
    systematic = sum(n_systematic),
    .by = domain
  ) |>
  arrange(domain) |>
  transmute(
    Domain = domain,
    `Cells in datasets that measure the variable` = fmt(cells),
    `With a value` = pct(value / cells),
    `Sporadic missing` = pct(sporadic / cells),
    `Systematic missing (wave never measured it)` = pct(systematic / cells)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: unknown
coverage |>
  filter(n_unknown > 0) |>
  summarise(unknown = sum(n_unknown), value = sum(n_value), datasets = n(), .by = variable_name) |>
  mutate(share = unknown / (unknown + value)) |>
  arrange(desc(unknown)) |>
  head(20) |>
  transmute(Variable = variable_name, `Unknown cells` = fmt(unknown), `Share of recorded cells` = pct(share), Datasets = datasets) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrr", caption = "The 20 variables with most `Unknown` cells.")
```

## Survey design

```{r}
#| label: design
design <- units |>
  summarise(
    rows = sum(rows),
    weight = sum(weight_rows),
    strata = sum(strata_rows),
    cluster = sum(cluster_rows),
    family = sum(family_rows),
    zero_weight = sum(weight_zero),
    trial = sum(trial_rows),
    .by = dataset_id
  )
has <- function(x) sum(x > 0)
tibble::tibble(
  `Design variable` = c("Survey weight", "Strata", "Cluster", "Family ID", "Trial arm"),
  Datasets = c(has(design$weight), has(design$strata), has(design$cluster), has(design$family), has(design$trial)),
  `Share of observations` = pct(c(sum(design$weight), sum(design$strata), sum(design$cluster), sum(design$family), sum(design$trial)) / sum(design$rows))
) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr")
```

Rows with a weight of zero: `r fmt(sum(design$zero_weight))`.

```{r}
#| label: weight-scale
units |>
  filter(weight_rows > 0) |>
  summarise(
    units = n(),
    smallest_mean = min(weight_mean),
    largest_mean = max(weight_mean),
    .by = dataset_id
  ) |>
  filter(units > 1) |>
  mutate(ratio = largest_mean / smallest_mean) |>
  arrange(desc(ratio)) |>
  head(15) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Units = units, `Largest unit mean weight / smallest` = signif(ratio, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr", caption = "Datasets whose mean weight differs most between units, which is why weights are normalised within unit.")
```

## What the data support

Datasets that hold both an exposure and at least one row of an outcome, anywhere in the dataset.
This is an upper bound: Step 7 counts rows where both are present for the same participant and wave.

```{r}
#| label: support
has_value <- coverage |> filter(n_value > 0) |> select(dataset_id, variable_name)
exposure_sets <- exposures |>
  filter(headline %in% TRUE) |>
  inner_join(has_value, by = "variable_name") |>
  distinct(exposure, dataset_id)
tree <- outcomes$tree
node_rows <- outcomes$rows |>
  filter(role == "outcome", use %in% c("core", "report"), !is.na(node)) |>
  inner_join(has_value, by = "variable_name") |>
  distinct(node, prereg_family, dataset_id)
node_support <- inner_join(node_rows, exposure_sets, by = "dataset_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = c(prereg_family, node, exposure))
node_support |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = exposure, values_from = datasets, values_fill = 0) |>
  left_join(tree[c("node", "label", "headline")], by = "node") |>
  arrange(prereg_family, label) |>
  mutate(Headline = ifelse(headline %in% TRUE, "yes", "")) |>
  select(Family = prereg_family, `Specific outcome` = label, Headline, everything(), -node, -headline) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: family-support
family_support <- inner_join(node_rows, exposure_sets, by = "dataset_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = c(prereg_family, exposure)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = exposure, values_from = datasets, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(prereg_family)
knitr::kable(family_support, caption = "Datasets per outcome family and headline exposure.")
```
